title: The Growing Challenge of Digital Identity Is Shaping IntegraTRACE’s Vision for Enterprise Visibility

content_html:
TL;DR

Every new application, API, and automated workflow adds identities that need oversight, yet most organizations lack a single source of truth for who has access to what. IntegraTRACE, founded by software engineer Steve Emmanuel, provides a SOC 2 Type II compliant identity visibility platform that centralizes human, non-human, and agentic identity data across cloud environments. The company is expanding from North America into Europe and Asia.

Enterprise technology has become significantly more interconnected over the past decade. Cloud platforms, automation, artificial intelligence, and software integrations have allowed organizations to operate with greater speed and flexibility, but they have also made understanding digital access far more complicated.

Every new application, automated workflow, and API introduces more identities with larger scope that require oversight, making visibility increasingly difficult as technology ecosystems continue to expand. A report shows that identity-based attacks accounted for nearly 1 in 3 intrusions observed in 2024, with attackers increasingly relying on valid accounts and stolen credentials as initial access methods.

Steve Emmanuel, CEO and founder of IntegraTRACE, witnessed that shift firsthand throughout more than a decade in software engineering. Beginning as a developer before advancing into technical leadership roles, he found that every step into larger organizations brought greater complexity. Teams expanded, cloud environments grew, and new applications were introduced, yet one challenge consistently remained.

“The biggest misconception is that somebody is keeping track of everything,” Emmanuel says. “Engineering assumes security has the answers. Security assumes engineering has the answers. Everyone believes someone has the complete picture, but very often there isn’t a reliable source of truth.”

Those experiences ultimately inspired the creation of IntegraTRACE, a SOC 2 Type II compliant identity visibility platform designed to help organizations understand how human, non-human, and agentic identities interact across cloud environments and enterprise applications. Rather than focusing solely on authentication or access management, Emmanuel explains that the company’s objective has been to provide organizations with a centralized view of digital identities as enterprise infrastructure becomes increasingly distributed.

From the beginning, Emmanuel wanted the platform to solve practical customer challenges rather than pursue features simply because they were popular. He explains that customer feedback has played a central role in product development, allowing the engineering team to respond quickly as cloud environments and identity ecosystems continue evolving.

According to Emmanuel, one of the most common responses from customers is realizing how much identity information had been dispersed across separate systems. Centralizing that information provides a clearer picture of access across the organization and helps surface potential risks before they become larger security concerns.

“Visibility changes the conversation,” Emmanuel says. “When organizations can see every identity and its level of access in one place, they gain insights that were previously difficult to obtain.”

From his perspective, customers frequently identify over-privileged accounts, dormant credentials, and permission structures that would have taken weeks or even months to uncover through manual reviews. Bringing those insights together into a centralized view allows security and engineering teams to spend less time gathering information and more time addressing potential risks.

IntegraTrace

He credits much of the company’s early growth to maintaining a close relationship with customers. Rather than following lengthy development roadmaps, the engineering team regularly incorporates customer feedback into the platform, often delivering requested improvements within weeks. Emmanuel believes that approach has helped ensure every product enhancement is tied to a practical business need.

“We’re building something people genuinely need,” he says. “When customers tell us there’s a problem slowing them down, we want to solve it quickly. That feedback continues to shape how the platform evolves.”

Looking ahead, Emmanuel says the company’s ambitions extend well beyond cloud infrastructure. Following early adoption across Canada and the United States, IntegraTRACE is preparing for expansion into Europe and Asia while broadening its visibility capabilities into HR systems, financial applications, and other enterprise software where identities continue to multiply.

His long-term vision is to make identity visibility a foundational layer across an organization’s technology ecosystem. As businesses continue adopting AI, automation, and increasingly connected applications, Emmanuel believes understanding digital access will become as important as managing the systems themselves.

“The organizations that adapt most successfully won’t necessarily be the ones with the most security tools,” Emmanuel says. “They’ll be the ones that have the clearest understanding of every identity operating across their business and the confidence to act on that knowledge.“

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

每个新的应用程序、API 和自动化工作流程都会添加需要监督的身份，但大多数组织缺乏单一的事实来源来确定谁可以访问什么内容。 IntegraTRACE 由软件工程师 Steve Emmanuel 创建，提供符合 SOC 2 Type II 标准的身份可见性平台，可跨云环境集中人类、非人类和代理身份数据。 该公司正在从北美扩展到欧洲和亚洲。

在过去的十年中，企业技术的互联性显着增强。 云平台、自动化、人工智能和软件集成使组织能够以更高的速度和灵活性运营，但也使理解数字访问变得更加复杂。

每个新的应用程序、自动化工作流程和 API 都会引入更多需要监督的更大范围的身份，随着技术生态系统的不断扩展，使得可见性变得越来越困难。 一份报告显示，2024 年观察到的入侵中，基于身份的攻击占近三分之一，攻击者越来越依赖有效帐户和被盗凭据作为初始访问方法。

IntegraTRACE 的首席执行官兼创始人 Steve Emmanuel 亲眼目睹了软件工程十多年来的这一转变。 在晋升为技术领导角色之前，他从一名开发人员开始，发现进入更大组织的每一步都会带来更大的复杂性。 团队规模不断扩大，云环境不断发展，新应用程序不断引入，但挑战始终存在。

“最大的误解是有人在跟踪一切，”伊曼纽尔说。 “工程假设安全性有答案。 安全性假设工程已经找到了答案。 每个人都相信某人掌握了完整的情况，但往往没有可靠的事实来源。”

这些经验最终激发了 IntegraTRACE 的创建，这是一个符合 SOC 2 Type II 的身份可见性平台，旨在帮助组织了解人类、非人类和代理身份如何跨云环境和企业应用程序进行交互。 Emmanuel 解释说，公司的目标不是仅仅关注身份验证或访问管理，而是随着企业基础设施变得越来越分散，为组织提供数字身份的集中视图。

从一开始，伊曼纽尔就希望该平台能够解决实际的客户挑战，而不是仅仅因为流行而追求功能。 他解释说，客户反馈在产品开发中发挥了核心作用，使工程团队能够随着云环境和身份生态系统的不断发展而快速响应。

伊曼纽尔表示，客户最常见的反应之一是意识到有多少身份信息分散在不同的系统中。 集中这些信息可以更清晰地了解整个组织的访问情况，并有助于在潜在风险成为更大的安全问题之前将其暴露出来。

“可见性改变了谈话，”伊曼纽尔说。 “当组织可以在一个地方看到每个身份及其访问级别时，他们就可以获得以前难以获得的见解。”

从他的角度来看，客户经常会发现特权过高的帐户、休眠凭证和权限结构，而通过人工审核需要数周甚至数月才能发现这些结构。 将这些见解整合到一个集中视图中，可以让安全和工程团队花更少的时间收集信息，而将更多的时间用于解决潜在风险。

集成跟踪

他将公司早期的发展归功于与客户保持密切的关系。 工程团队没有遵循冗长的开发路线图，而是定期将客户反馈纳入平台，通常在几周内提供所需的改进。 伊曼纽尔认为，这种方法有助于确保每项产品增强都与实际业务需求挂钩。

“我们正在打造人们真正需要的东西，”他说。 “当客户告诉我们有问题拖慢他们的速度时，我们希望尽快解决。 这种反馈将继续影响平台的发展。”

展望未来，伊曼纽尔表示，公司的雄心远远超出了云基础设施领域。 继在加拿大和美国早期采用之后，IntegraTRACE 正准备扩展到欧洲和亚洲，同时将其可见性能力扩展到人力资源系统、财务应用程序和其他身份不断倍增的企业软件。

他的长期愿景是使身份可见性成为整个组织技术生态系统的基础层。 随着企业继续采用人工智能、自动化和日益互联的应用程序，伊曼纽尔相信了解数字访问将变得与管理系统本身一样重要。

“适应最成功的组织不一定是拥有最多安全工具的组织，”伊曼纽尔说。 “他们将最清楚地了解其业务中运作的每个身份，并有信心根据这些知识采取行动。”
